rv.q: The one thing it isn’t, perhaps, is suitable for younger children. The National’s age guidance is 8+ but 15+ might be wiser. In this telling, the princess (Rosie Graham) is sent to sleep for a century by an inept fairy (Lisa Lambe, excellent).
Yet it's also often glorious, even if it reminds us perhaps once too many times that its better to be yourself rather than a hero or a villain in a fairy tale.

Instead, this is an elaborate gingerbread castle of a show that's built on candyfloss-light foundations: lovely to look at, undeniably impressive, but doomed to collapse under the weight of its own overweening ambition.
The book, by Tanya Ronder, is befuddling, the music by Jim Fortune erratic, and Norris’ lyrics trite and toe-curling: a woeful mess that the most potent magic couldn’t save.

This musical adaptation of Sleeping Beauty played only a handful of its planned performances last December due to Covid surges, and finally arrives at its official opening, a whole year later, as a sporadically charming but utterly confused mess.
In the final reckoning, Hex delivers on musical theatre’s central proposition – it entertains.

For any fantasy and fairytale lovers, Hex is a welcome twist on the genre, giving us all permission to create worlds within our imaginations and find solace and sympathy in the most unexpected of places.

It’s great to see it get its full airing, but that extra time could have been wisely spent in reviewing the work to make sure, ultimately, it actually makes sense rather than just looking spectacular.
Hex is an enjoyable family show, but is frustratingly bogged down by certain elements to be a real success.

Certainly there's middle-of-the-road, untaxing entertainment here, but it is not tight, clever, significant, noteworthy or especially magical, which is perhaps the greatest disappointment given the subject, the stage and the time taken to deliver the production.
In spite of the splashy spectacle and sets, it’s all a bit of a jumble.

cn.t: Visually stunning but narratively confused, this long-delayed Sleeping Beauty reimagining dazzles with inventive design yet stumbles with a meandering story and uneven songs that never fully cohere.
